correspondence.component_scope: headward opening and northwest bend
correspondence.finding: The selected mountainous opening lies on the mapped Trail Creek corridor west of High Lake. Its initial westward and northwestward reach, broad turn, and subsequent southeastward valley course have continuous cartographic correspondence. The name is read on the selected creek corridor, not inferred solely from membership in a basin.
correspondence.correspondence: Positive original-map correspondence at ordinary component/corridor scale.

correspondence.component_scope: middle Trail Creek and contributing High Lake link
correspondence.finding: The selected southeastward Trail Creek valley continues past the mapped tributary connection from the High Lake outlet corridor. High Lake is an off-selected contributing lake: the selected line does not traverse its lake surface. The map shows that link and the continuing downstream creek channel at ordinary corridor scale.
correspondence.correspondence: Positive original-map correspondence at ordinary component/corridor scale.

correspondence.component_scope: Trail Creek to Izavieknik River below Upper Togiak Lake
correspondence.finding: The selected lower Trail Creek corridor connects to the Izavieknik River corridor below the outlet of Upper Togiak Lake. The maps distinguish the Upper Togiak Lake outlet arm from the selected creek approach. Upper Togiak Lake is a contributing lake link, not a selected through-passage.
correspondence.correspondence: Positive original-map correspondence at ordinary component/corridor scale.

correspondence.component_scope: Izavieknik River and Togiak Lake inlet
correspondence.finding: From the junction below Upper Togiak Lake the selected route follows the continuous, locally multichannel Izavieknik valley southward into the northeastern head of Togiak Lake. Both the named river corridor and actual lake inlet connection are visible.
correspondence.correspondence: Positive original-map correspondence at ordinary component/corridor scale.

correspondence.component_scope: Togiak Lake passage and southwest outlet
correspondence.finding: The selected route traverses the elongated southwest-trending Togiak Lake and leaves its southwestern end through the mapped Togiak River outlet. West Togiak Lake and its West Creek connection form a separately mapped western side link, not the selected through-lake route. Additional lateral tributary inlets and the outlet channel are visible; no shoreline-vertex precision is asserted.
correspondence.correspondence: Positive original-map correspondence at ordinary component/corridor scale.

correspondence.component_scope: upper and middle Togiak River
correspondence.finding: The selected river continues south from the lake, passes the east-side Ongivinuk tributary setting, then bends west through the mapped Togiak River corridor. The overlapping maps distinguish the north-fed Narogurum and Kashaiak junctions from the selected trunk and show its following southwest turn. These names identify local tributary settings, not extra selected mainstems.
correspondence.correspondence: Positive original-map correspondence at ordinary component/corridor scale.

correspondence.component_scope: lower river and major tributary mouths
correspondence.finding: The selected southwestward lower corridor is continuously mapped as Togiak River, with Pungokepuk Creek entering from the east and Gechiak Creek from the west. The route then crosses the broad lowland with side channels, wetlands and meanders toward the coast. A representative system candidate does not rename these tributaries.
correspondence.correspondence: Positive original-map correspondence at ordinary component/corridor scale.

correspondence.component_scope: actual terminal
correspondence.finding: The mapped Togiak River reaches the tidal/coastal opening at the northern head of Togiak Bay beside Togiak and west of Twin Hills. This is the actual terminal setting of the selected line. It is distinguished from the separate neighboring Ungalikthluk coastal drainage and bay. The correspondence is at ordinary estuary/corridor scale, without an exact bank or mouth-point claim.
correspondence.correspondence: Positive original-map correspondence at ordinary component/corridor scale.

correspondence.component_scope: Opening and first interior corridor
correspondence.finding: The opening lies well inland from the southwest coast in the national original’s Inland Ice field. The westward and southwestward initial portions remain within mapped ice terrain. Regional Sheet 2 does not extend far enough east to supply this opening; the national original provides continuous geographic coverage at its published generalized scale.
correspondence.correspondence: Complete selected terrain correspondence at generalized scale; no natural-river or hydraulic-continuity inference.

correspondence.component_scope: Entire middle ice corridor and southern bend
correspondence.finding: The long middle westward run and southerly bend remain in the mapped southwest Inland Ice before the selected line approaches the coastal ice/rock margin. National and regional cartography overlap at the western part. Ice contours and subsurface-geology lines were read according to the legends and not treated as river channels or tributaries.
correspondence.correspondence: Complete selected terrain correspondence at generalized scale; no natural-river or hydraulic-continuity inference.

correspondence.component_scope: Lower westward-to-northwestward turn
correspondence.finding: The regional original resolves ice adjoining the exposed coastal rock terrain north of Frederikshåbs Isblink and east of inner Bjørnesund. The selected lower turn traverses this ice/rock-margin setting toward the fjord head; the map does not label the selected sequence as one natural river.
correspondence.correspondence: Complete selected terrain correspondence at generalized scale; no natural-river or hydraulic-continuity inference.

correspondence.component_scope: Actual selected terminal setting
correspondence.finding: The selected end corresponds at ordinary generalized scale to the inner, northeastern Bjørnesund ice/rock-margin and fjord-head setting. The regional map depicts the enclosing exposed-rock land and neighboring ice as well as the fjord context. The terminal is not promoted to a surveyed ordinary river mouth, and the fjord name is not promoted to a river name.
correspondence.correspondence: Complete selected terrain correspondence at generalized scale; no natural-river or hydraulic-continuity inference.

correspondence.component_scope: Major branches, lakes/reservoirs and selected-component scope
correspondence.finding: All selected geometry belongs to FID 8910. The source review follows the opening, entire modeled corridor, lower terrain transition and ending. No additional selected branch FID or named river-to-lake/reservoir connector is established by these original maps for this object; modeled segment joins are not treated as observed tributary junctions.
correspondence.correspondence: Complete selected terrain correspondence at generalized scale; no natural-river or hydraulic-continuity inference.

correspondence.component_scope: Huayacocotla headward approach and northward Vinazco turn
correspondence.finding: The Huayacocotla original depicts the selected western/headward approach east and southeast of the town, joining the locally labelled Viñazco corridor before its northward bend along the Texcatepec side. The regional sheet overlaps this setting near El Manzano. This is ordinary headward-corridor correspondence, not a claim that the model’s first point is a surveyed named spring. The short opening is left without a separately established hydronym; nearby Prieto, Mezquite, Toluca and other tributary labels are not applied uniformly to it.
correspondence.correspondence: complete at ordinary headward and connecting-corridor scale; first-reach name unresolved

correspondence.component_scope: Texcatepec and Tlachichilco upper/middle Vinazco
correspondence.finding: The regional original and the Texcatepec Relieve map follow the northeast/eastward river along the northern Texcatepec setting. The latter directly labels Viñazco and distinguishes the Atixtaca approach from the south. The Tlachichilco original overlaps the northern continuation toward the Benito Juárez/Ixhuatlán de Madero side while distinguishing Zacualpan, Obscuro and Chiflón branches. These overlapping corridors account for the selected northeast course; the separate southern branches are not substituted for the selected Vinazco.
correspondence.correspondence: complete overlapping corridor and material branch distinction

correspondence.component_scope: Ixhuatlán de Madero–Tzocohuite–Chapopote Núñez Vinazco corridor
correspondence.finding: The regional map visibly continues the western Vinazco east past the Tzicatlán/Tlachichilco setting, north of Ixhuatlán de Madero, then northeast through the Tzocohuite and Mesa de Calcote side toward Chapopote Núñez. Its connected channel is the selected western approach. The Álamo Temapache original overlaps the lower part and labels Viñazco on that southwestern incoming river. This establishes the middle transfer geographically rather than from the basin table or model connectivity.
correspondence.correspondence: complete ordinary middle-corridor correspondence

correspondence.component_scope: Vinazco–Pantepec junction upstream of Álamo and fragment continuation
correspondence.finding: The regional original shows the Pantepec approaching independently from the south through the San Martín/Metlaltoyuca side and joining the Vinazco upstream of Álamo. The Álamo municipal map shows the incoming Viñazco and the continuous eastward lower river labelled Tuxpam. The selected route takes the western Vinazco approach, passes the junction and continues into that lower river across the two retained FIDs. The fragment boundary is not treated as a cartographic or legal naming boundary; the southern Pantepec headwaters are not part of this selected path.
correspondence.correspondence: complete material confluence and connected lower-river transition

correspondence.component_scope: Álamo–Higueral–Santiago de la Peña lower Tuxpan
correspondence.finding: The Álamo and Tuxpan originals overlap the selected meandering eastward river past Álamo and the Higueral setting into the urban Tuxpan–Santiago de la Peña reach. Álamo’s map uses Tuxpam; the downstream municipal map uses Tuxpan. Both depict the same connected lower river in the regional context. Buenavista, Miquetla and Tecomate are separately drawn tributaries; their labels are not used to rename all selected portions. No selected lake or reservoir passage is required by these originals.
correspondence.correspondence: complete lower-river corridor with overlapping municipal coverage

correspondence.component_scope: Tuxpan port and actual Gulf of Mexico mouth
correspondence.finding: The Tuxpan Relieve map carries the broad river east/northeast beside the urban reach directly through the coastal-bar setting into the Golfo de México. The regional original independently depicts Barra de Túxpam/Puerto Tuxpam and the same outlet. Tampamachoco lies north of the lower river and the Tumilco estero lies south; the selected route follows the river mouth rather than a crossing of either adjacent waterbody. ASIPONA’s normally read infrastructure page independently names Río Tuxpan and its Gulf mouth. The generalized final seaward extension is accounted for by this ordinary river-mouth corridor, without matching a precise inlet point, jetty end or dated shoreline.
correspondence.correspondence: complete actual river-mouth and sea-terminal setting

correspondence.component_scope: Selected opening and upper feeder
correspondence.finding: The selected opening lies on the mapped westward headward branch in the Jatunsayuna setting, leading into the Ayrampillo/Orccococha drainage. The stream and lake-linked continuation are read on the original Chaviña sheet at ordinary corridor scale; no precise source-point claim or independent opening hydronym is made.
correspondence.correspondence: Positive original-map correspondence at ordinary component/corridor scale.

correspondence.component_scope: Pallcarana and Ancascocha passage
correspondence.finding: From the Orccococha setting the mapped route continues south through the Pallcarana corridor, by the Totorcca/Chiyunco setting, into the northwestern side of Laguna Ancascocha. The selected continuation leaves the southern lake outlet and proceeds through the Sangarara valley near Chaviña. Names on side feeders and lakes are not assigned to the entire selected object.
correspondence.correspondence: Positive original-map correspondence at ordinary component/corridor scale.

correspondence.component_scope: Sangarara and westward transition
correspondence.finding: The lake-outlet corridor receives the western Chaviña tributary and continues south. The adjacent Coracora sheet carries the same valley west of Coracora and Sanquipampa, then shows the selected westward bend toward the Lampalla valley. Northern and eastern tributaries remain distinct from the selected continuation.
correspondence.correspondence: Positive original-map correspondence at ordinary component/corridor scale.

correspondence.component_scope: Lampalla middle valley and Palca junction
correspondence.finding: The westward valley across the Coracora/Jaqui sheet join continues into the broader middle corridor through the Campo Santo–Palca/Angostura setting. The northern Pararmayo valley joins there; the selected main route turns southwest toward San Luis. The connected Para/Sancos tributary settings on the upstream sheet are separately shown.
correspondence.correspondence: Positive original-map correspondence at ordinary component/corridor scale.

correspondence.component_scope: Yauca lower inland valley
correspondence.finding: The selected valley proceeds southwest through San Luis and Jaqui, past the eastern Acaville-side junction, then south through the El Faro/La Calera, Andenes, Mochica and Lampilla settings. The Chala sheet and western Acarí–Yauca sheet jointly establish the continuing lower valley; a map-edge break is not treated as a missing river connection.
correspondence.correspondence: Positive original-map correspondence at ordinary component/corridor scale.

correspondence.component_scope: Actual terminal corridor
correspondence.finding: The mapped lower river passes Quincao/San Fernando and the town of Yauca, crosses the coastal road at Puente de Yauca, and reaches the Pacific through its alluvial coastal outlet. INGEMMET and the independently prepared IGP coastal map agree on this ordinary terminal setting. No precise bank, mouth vertex or modern braiding geometry is asserted.
